During gameplay, the whole of the board is seen. The dart cursor swirls around the screen, can be controlled in a limited fashion and is released by pressing fire.

157252.overview: Zeppelin's second game licensed from the successful darts player has a much wider scope than the previous Jocky Wilson's Darts Challenge. The control system involves directing a hand which guides the dart, but this is constantly moving in a random arc, reflecting realistic jitters but making accurate aiming difficult at first. The standard 501 darts rules are among the six games included. The other games include variants loosely based on football (hit the bulls-eye to start scoring, then a double adds one goal to your score) and bowls (in which a 'jack' dart is thrown by one player, and the aim is to get your darts as close to it as possible). There are also Ten-Dart century (score exactly 100 with 10 darts), Shanghai (where only darts thrown at a particular area can score) and Scram (where one player shoots to successively knock sectors out of play, and the opponent must score as much as possible from the others).

157254.overview: Joe is a platform game created by MR-Soft and released in both Computronic 1987/03-04, and in Magic Disk 64 1988/05. In it you play the dog Joe, who must avoid the alligators, piranha fish and other baddies like the birdie, cuttie (scissors) and jumper and make your way across the board, turning all the tiles green in order to get to the next level.

157255.overview: Rare to see an 8-bit, single person platform game from Norway. Programmed by Svein A. Berg in 1985 and released by Datacompaniet. Take Joe over the stile, get all the keys and get back to the safe without being caught by the guards. use joystick or key: CTRL for left, arrow left for down, 1 for up, 2 for right and space for jump. Press a key and get playing! Choose Factory for a game creation kit for this game.

157256.overview: A Hungarian 2 Player only shooter\dueling game. The game has an unknown developer, it was released by Puhasoft, but the year is not known as of now.

157259.overview: As Players Software correctly predicted, London in 1995 is an unfriendly unsafe city ran by thugs. Innocent civilians who leave the house will almost certainly face violence. An acclaimed hero since his successes in the original, Joe Blade is the man to put things right - if he can kill 100 thugs and rescue 20 civilians within ten minutes, the thugs will retreat and the city will be saved. As Joe, you must move through the streets and kill these thugs, by kicking them in the head (they have body armour). As in the first game, the streets are flick-screen and have many doorways linking them. Rescuing civilians involves touching them before completing a sub-game within a minute. There are four subgame variants of increasing difficulty, all based around a 1-2-3-4 sequence of numbers. The first involves simply stopping the cursor as each one appears in order - pressing the wrong one sends you back to having to find a 1. In the second, the numbers are on screen in random order, a cursor cycling through them - press fire to swap the two numbers currently highlighted. In the third, you are presented with two jumbled sets and must put one of them in order, by swapping numbers across the two sets. In the fourth, you must form the sequence by swapping an ever-changing number into the right place, by pressing fire at the right moment.

157261.overview: Your investigations start outisde of the old Anderson Mansion, but will you be able to do your duty to find the files that will crack this one open AND still get out alive?

157267.overview: You, Joe AKA: Joe The Whizz kid, are are stuck in a shop.  This store has a few different areas for you to walk through like a food section and a hardware section. If it floats or moves along the floor avoid it, make your way to the end of the level unscathed to continue.

157268.overview: In John Elway's Quarterback, it's one player vs. the computer or two human players going head-to-head in single-game American football action. Select your team's home city (there is no NFL or NFLPA license, so there are no real teams or players) and then battle the opposing team for four 15-minute (accelerated real-time) quarters. Graphics are simple: one team has blue uniforms, the other team red ones. The human player gets control of the quarterback on offense and the middle linebacker on defense. The play perspective is top-down and vertical-scrolling. Choose from 9 offensive--mostly passing--plays and 6 defensive plays. Teams have 9 players each.

157269.overview:
John Lowe won the World Darts Championship twice, and puts his name to this combination of darts-based games. There are 10 difficulty levels to take on. Only part of the board is on screen at a time, with the screen scrolling as you move the arrow from your perspective. This makes some targets much harder to hit than others.

A practice mode is included, alongside standard 501 and round-the-board games, plus variants loosely based around soccer and cricket. In the former, the player who scores higher with each set of 3 darts gains territory (so in reality it’s more like US Football). The cricket variant sees players alternate in batting and bowling roles – in the former points are converted to runs; in the latter, hit the bullseye to get batsmen out.

157289.overview: In this horizontal shooter you fly your B27 jet across the city and blast down the enemy planes before you end up being blasted down from the skies. Have fun.

157291.overview: Old american football simulation co-designed by famous sportscaster John Madden. The first game in EA's long-running Madden series. Different versions of this game have been available on almost every platform - with the Mega Drive version being the most famous of them all. The game concentrates more on tactics than pure action.

157292.overview: Johnny Reb is a turn-based strategy game for one or two players, based on the American Civil War. Players can control an army of either the Union or the Confederation. There are three types of units: infantry, cavalry and artillery, and it's possible to decide how many of each type the player's army should consist of. After the initial set-up, the battlefield is generated. The goal is to capture the enemy's flag, but it's also possible to achieve a victory by points. Army control is handled with the keyboard - units can move in eight directions. Artillery can shoot over distance, the other unit types can directly attack by simply moving to an adjacent square.

157293.overview: Based on the American Civil War, Johnny Reb II is a one or two player strategy game. After the title screen a menu appears allowing you limited tinkering of the game's parameters. You can also choose which side you want to play as. Once you are happy with your choices the game begins. The game is viewed overhead of the terrain with your and the enemies' forces shown as icons. Moving the cursor with your joystick, you can highlight an icon and get details about that unit. On the right of the screen different icons appear showing the type of orders that are available. Some icons can make other icons appear allowing you to elaborate each order.

157294.overview:
Aussie Joker Poker is a point scoring card game for 2-90 players.

Each player is dealt a hand of five cards, and the hand is scored according to poker hand value, card value, and the suits involved.

After being dealt a hand, the player is displayed a score. The player can risk discarding cards to acquire a better hand, but if the point value is lessened, the player busts, and they forfeit points for that hand. The player can keep risking drawing new cards to improve their hand until they bust or are satisfied with their score.

Card are selecting using the numbers one to five, and they are graphically displayed on the screen. There is an option to display who the current leading hand is each round, and the score to beat. The player can define the number of rounds per game.

157295.overview: After three months at sea, you Jolly Jack have been given shore leave for the night and your aim is to get drunk, have sex with a woman before getting safely back to your ship. You have 50 pounds in your pocket and you have to explore the town, Sharksville to fulfill your needs. Jolly Jack's Run Ashore is a adventure where text on the screen describes your surroundings and you type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your location.

157296.overview: Puzzler in which you have to push tiled letters around to make a word, placed where the arrowed tile is, in order to complete each level. A bit sore on the eyes with the background scrolling. Created by Thomas Koncina and published in Game On 1993/04-05.

157297.overview:
Journey to the Centre of Eddie Smith's Head is a traditional text adventure made using the Quill adventure generation software from Gilsoft. You tell the game what you want to do via a textual interface and the parser is based on verb / noun input.

Scientific genius Eddie Smith is working on a new and improved atomic bomb for the British government when he hits his head on a nuclear reactor in the laboratory. Able to remember his mission, in his post-concussion state he thinks he should use the weapon on his own country. The player is in the shoes of one of Eddies colleagues, and the task is to search the research complex and the near lying city and eventually hunt down the irrational genius and thwart his plan.

157298.overview: 11 of the world's most valuable treasures are hidden in underground caverns. Some are easily found, others require a lot of skill to recover. Beware the giant lizards, vampire bats and trolls. You can dodge some things, and shoot others. There are hundreds of tunnels to explore and a whole host of wonders to discover.

157299.overview: Just another day for Judge Dredd in Mega City One as he fights crime and tries to return the city back to some normality. You play the Judge as he tries to attempt six missions of crime. Once a mission is completed there is a bonus level related to the last mission to attempt. Take too long to complete a mission and the crime rate rises. Let the rate get too high and it's game over. To aid the Judge you have various weapons to fire and also your Lawmaster bike. This allows you to move around faster but you can't fire your weapon or arrest people thus making the crime rate rise. Judge Dredd is a side view platform game that scrolls as you move left or right. Pressing the space bar allows you to change from walking to riding your bike. The joystick controls your character while the fire button shoots your weapon.

157300.overview: Help your young one, ages 3 to 6 increase their preschool skills. In Juggles' Rainbow you find and easy, colorful  program that teaches up\down, left/right and pre-reading skills. It is the perfect way to get your child started on the computer.

157301.overview:
Jukebox is a musical strategy game that's kind of a cross between a chess match and a dance contest. During the game the Jukebox is jumpin' with lots of terrific songs. Songs so good you never want them to stop. But to keep the music playing you've got to create gold records. Using your dancing feet and your natural sense of rhythm you jump from square to square creating hit records as you go. Aim for the pulsating gold tiles, because you can build them into records. And the more gold records you get the more coins you earn. Use the coins to keep the music bopping and the game from stopping. Play against the computer or another player. 
But plan your strategy carefully, because in Jukebox you can box yourself in - and then the music's over.

157312.overview: Jumbo Lander is a game similar to Lunar Lander, except instead of successfully landing on the moon the player must try to land a jumbo jet. The game plays in turns and each turn the player must input the new desired climb rate and thrust. On screen information include the climb rate, acceleration, velocity, altitude, distance to runway and runway left, and an image of a jumbo jet.

157317.overview: Mind the gaps in this run and jump game for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by Roger Svensson and published by Computer Boss International (CBI) in 1984.

157318.overview: Large maze arcade game published in both Loadstar #006 and in the "Maze Madness" game pack.

157319.overview:
A shoot'em up, space invaders style game published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/11 (Issue #17). Fire your laser and defend your planet from 
the invading Ryiads. 

"jump!" pits you against an invader who's trying to blast both you and your planet. He's wily and you must use your laser in defense. When you hit the invader, a Ryiad, you get 50 points and 25 energy units. When a Ryiad shot hits the surface of your planet, the point of impact is illustrated by reversing the damaged character. When he hits it a second time, a crater is formed. If he hits the same spot a third time, it disappears and you lose 25 points. 

You can move over the undamaged and slightly damaged areas of the surface, but you lose a turn if you try to move over craters or pits. Shift-Z or Shift-C  to jump left or right over those.

157320.overview: In this puzzle game you jump the color of your opponent as though you were playing checkers\droughts. If you can jump multiple times the better! Jump more than your oppenent and you win! Many starting scenarios to choose from. Published in Magic Disk 64 1991/07, Magic Disk 64 GE 1992/1, and also in Abo Disk #4.

157322.overview: The ultimate climbing and jumping game is here! With the most amazing game editor, so you can build and play your own games.

157323.overview: A Frogger clone from Livewire Software. As usual, your goal is to safely guide the frog across the road, avoiding the cars, jumping on the turtles and tree trunks across the river and land safely in one of the five slots on the other shore. The C64 and MSX versions add a pseudo-isometric effect to the graphics, as well as a female frog and an insect to be eaten for bonus points. After all five slots are filled up, the gameplay repeats, but faster.

157324.overview:
Jumpin' Jimmy is a platform game where you control a kangaroo attempting to collect fruit and baby kangaroos over four levels. Each level scrolls left or right when you move and at the start of a level the screen scrolls and you move the joystick to allow your kangaroo to fall to the nearest platform. There are various creatures moving about each level and if they touch you, you lose one of four lives. Falling from any height will also kill you, but you can jump down a certain height. Scattered around each level are various objects which can help or hinder you and these include stars to transport you elsewhere on a level, elevators and objects that make platforms disappear. As well as the main playing area there is also a radar at the top of the screen showing the location of all collectable objects. Up to four players can play and each player takes it in turn when the last player has been killed. Also included with the game is a construction set which allows you to create your own levels.

This is essentially inspired by the old Sun Electronics arcade game, Kangaroo.

157325.overview: This is a simultaneous competitive 2 player only platformer and a clone of the ZX Spectrum game of the same name. The objective is to get to the top of the screen, running to avoid a gap opening beneath you and jumping up when a gap cycles above you, thus completing the level. Published in Game On 1991/12.

157326.overview: JumpJets is a nicely done isometric-viewed shoot 'em up, reminiscent of Zaxxon but in a more open environment. You fly over the isles of the sea taking out fuel tanks, choppers, planes and even patrol boats that protect the seas between the islands. If you can make it past the first stage you can plan your refuel and rearmament landing on the carrier, but you must have nerves of steel and catlike reflexes to land your jet and get back into the fight.

157328.overview: This particular jungle will haunt your dreams by the time you will have explored all 14 levels of the game. paf of your almost impossible mission is to find the key. Further details about your mysterious task will gradually be let known as you bravely meet the perils of man-eating plants, spiders, skeletons and many more.

157329.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter that feels reminiscent Moon Patrol, collect fuel by shooting fuel and avoid the aliens shooting at you.  Written by Konrad Wieclawski and published in Game On 1990/01.

157331.overview: You are code-named Orion, an adolescent agent of ACT (the Adventure Connection Team), summoned straight out of the hallways of your high school by Max Huntington to participate in a mission taking you to the darkest jungles of Africa, to locate and defuse the limitless energies stored in an alien artifact there before sinister competing agents of BRUTE (the Bureau of Random Unlawful Terror and Evil) beat you to it! Other members of your team include an archaeologist ("Digger"), an environmental scientist ("Erda"), a nuclear engineer ("Celeste") and Olano, your guide. You, of course, are the computer expert, and your skills will be put to the test, typing in included BASIC programs to decrypt secret messages, weigh tolerances, plot courses through labyrinths and calculate necessary angles of deflection. The abilities of the whole team will be called for to overcome natural obstacles, untrusting natives, the sapping effects of the Devorim Force, BRUTE agents, a traitor in your midst, the perils and traps of the golden lost city containing the artifact, and the deadly artifact itself! Though the story shares the dynamic 2nd-person perspective ("You try to talk, but you cannot make a sound") of Choose-Your-Own-Adventures, the text (like most books) is a non-interactive fixed-rail trip of zero interactivity -- however, some of the type-in programs included offer numerous outcomes, moving into the "game" field what might otherwise be best categorized as an elaborate set-up for low-impact programming exercises. An appendix is included describing how to modify the BASIC program listings for greatest compatibility with 10 of the most popular home microcomputer BASICs, as well as describing what each program does and how it works. Hey! You got your education in my adventure!

157333.overview: Published in Radio Elettronica & Computer 1988/10 and as part of Bogies Pick Value Pack 5. Dropped behind enemy lines George Chesthair must battle against the baddies and in the long cherished style of old...shoot the hell out of anything that moves! You need fast reactions, digital dexterity and all the other cliched things they always write about in scenarios like this. Good luck! I think at this point I'm supposed to say in a deep and meaningful style....YOU'LL NEED IT.

157334.overview: Jungle Story is a side view horizontal scrolling game where you move Mowgli around the bottom half of the screen, avoiding animals and spears over various levels while the screen scrolls constantly from left to right. The spears appear from the left of the screen while the animals which are elephants and snakes appear from the right and they have to be avoided or you lose one of three lives. Moneys also make an appearance in the trees above and drop coconuts and these also need avoiding. To move off a level you have to kill five tigers that run across the screen very fast by throwing pots of fire to kill them.

157339.overview: An educational word game. Offers hundreds of words that every child needs to recognize easily. Getting down to learning a tricky subject can become a good deal easier when there's an element of fun involved.

157340.overview: Junkyard Jalopies is a flick-screen platformer where you have to move around two screens per level to collect car parts to finish a car on the bottom left of the first screen. Before you collect car parts you first have to get to the junkyard from the left to the right of the screen, jumping over tyres. Each screen is made up of five levels (with an extra one at the bottom of the screen), and you have to use lifts to go up and down the levels while avoiding creatures and moving objects. If you hit a tyre, creature or object, fall down a level, or allow the timer to reach zero then you lose one of six lives. Spread over each level are car parts to build the car and there are also bombs that can be collected. To complete a level you have two choices, build the car before the timer reaches zero or collect the bombs to reset the timer before building the car. Your hero is constantly moving and when you collect a car part you take it to the unfinished car to place it in the correct place to receive money. Once the car is built then you drive away before seeing an animated scene of you selling it for money. You then move to the next level with more creatures and objects with more bombs and car parts on the screen.

157341.overview: Can you navigate the rocking outcroppings and vicious stalagmites to find a safe landing?

157355.overview: Jupiter Mission contains elements of graphics/text adventure, space war role-playing and arcade joystick games. The different elements in Jupiter Mission are tied together by a story line. Government agents drag you from your home early on a cold January morning and put you in charge of a solo mission to Jupiter. The game's story is then furthered by graphic adventure elements and the player does different arcade sequences, such as shooting asteroids to keep from being damaged, landing on a moon, and exploring.

157357.overview: A bilingual program for learning over 500 usefule and up to date French words. There are five vocabulary areas: Travel , People, Shopping, Food and Drink, and Essentials. Word from English into French or visa versa with a choice of games or key-in options.

157358.overview: Create and write your own Animated stories using 9 Scenes, 48 Objects and 25 Animations.

160088.overview: Based on the novel by James Herbert, The Rats is a game combining strategy elements and a text adventure as you control various characters in the battle to control and kill a huge swarm of rats overrunning London. If the rats spread further than London into the rest of Britain then it is game over. You start the game as Foskins looking at a map of London with white squares flashing showing reported sightings of rats. Here you can see the report, deploy forces or enable research with Howard.

160106.overview: Vegas Jackpot is a simulation of the gambling fruit machine. The player tosses the coin in the slot of the video machine and starts to spin the reels, waiting for the winning combination to appear for a single-pay line. To increase the chances, it is possible to hold certain reels or to nudge them for a certain number of times when it is allowed. The goal of the game is to win jackpots. The amount of reels in the video machine is equal to three for ZX Spectrum, BBC / Electron and Dragon 32/64 versions, and to four for other versions

160337.overview:
Endorsed by famous tennis player, Jimmy Connors, this game offers tournament and single play on multiple court types.

Using crosshairs, aim your ball to the other side of the court and hope you hit where you want. If you are lucky, you might even score an Ace. If not, you will need to be ready to return your opponent's return. Run back and forth as you try to keep hitting the ball over the net until your opponent misses, or you do. When you hit the ball, you will want to attempt changing the direction and speed of the ball to throw your opponent off balance. This is the real challenge of any tennis game.

160389.overview: A Q-Bert style game where they didn't even try to make Q-Bert look like a frog to match the name change. Strangely, not a bad version to play.

160390.overview:
A Norwegian adventure game created in 1984 by Norace Computing using the Quill Adventure Writer System. MESSAGE FROM THE MANAGEMENT:
WELCOME TO JUNGLE HUNTING. WE HOPE YOU WILL ENJOY THIS STORY GAME FOR MANY NIGHTS TO COME. Mr. Zabixu hopes that you are comfortable - and wants to stay as long as possible.-- Yes, in reality he hopes that you will be among the many guests who actually NEVER feel like they can leave him!! 
 
You are standing in the hall of Ogabwo Manor. In your subconscious, there is something that tells you that strange things have happened. Isn't this where the "JUNGLE PIRATE" Zabixu once lived? A smattering of dust and cobwebs lies everywhere. A silent wall clock with an opening that says half-timber. The evening sun sparkles a tray of silver! A recently written note lies on the table next to it...Will be back at five o'clock. What now?

168186.overview:
Jabato is an adventure composed of six parts, each one with its own independent argument, but subtly related to the main plot. In each geographic area you will have different problems, interlaced within a series of "custom pictures" which gather part of Europe and North Africa as they were in the first century BC. It was the time of the Roman Empire splendor, their legions extend and dominate the known world, but in each one of their provinces the inhabitants breathe freedom and make their own rules, codes and rituals. In Hispania, Jabato became a legendary figure, prototype of the implacable hero in the fight against the evil but with a great heart. In this history you will assume the role of this fabulous personage.

But it won't be easy: instead of living one of his moments of greatness, you will incarnate a defeated Jabato, without friends, prisoner in a dirty Roman jail with the bitter feeling that his beloved Claudia is captive in a distant land. Your final mission will be to avoid having her sacrificed by the fanatical sect of the Egyptian sub-world. For it, on the first part, you must liberate yourself from the Roman yoke and search for company. Multiple adventures are awaiting you soon in the Galia and Hispania. The second part begins in Cesarea, in which you must enter in the heart of Africa and obtain the keys that could allow you to survive in the lands of the mythical tombs, sacred Pharaohs and great mysteries. If you survive, you will fight the final battle against the terrible forces of the dark wisdom.

168239.overview:
Developed by Leigh White of Throwback Games, Jam It is an arcade style 2-on-2 basketball game for the Commodore 64, featuring the most intense sports action and entertainment ever crammed into 64K!

Do you get confused by complex button combinations in modern basketball video games? In Jam It, just one button with your control stick is enough to make extreme dunks, jump-shots, blocks, passes, post-up plays, and steals!

Jam It supports 1-4 simultaneous players (via the Protovision 4-player adapter) and features opponents with realistic and challenging AI, 4 difficulty levels, 3 unlockable bonuses, in-game on-screen commentary, comprehensive statistics and even a halftime show mini-game!


    Supports 1-4 simultaneous players!
    Realistic and challenging AI!
    4 difficulty levels!
    3 unlockable bonuses!
    In-game commentary!
    Halftime show mini-game
    Comprehensive statistics
    PAL & NTSC compatibility!

168354.overview: Johnny is a platform game with twenty single-screen levels. The player takes on the role of Snoopy , the dog from the comic series Peanuts. In each level the player must walk from left to right with Snoopy, while avoiding various dangers. After all twenty levels have been played, the game starts again, but now with a higher playing speed.

168355.overview:
For many years this was the only squash game in existence, and it's licensed by one of the top stars of the 80s. Jonah calls the score, and claimed that the program could boost a player's squash skills, as well as provide entertainment.

Jonah Barrington's Squash features one and two player modes, with 4 difficulty levels. Accurate rebounds are implemented, and the ball's bounce is visible from its shadow. Realistic tactics appear to produce the correct effects, in terms of playing attacking or defensive.

168397.overview: A platform game created in 1985 and also published in Compute mit 1985/05. The loincloth wearing jungle man you control can only jump in one direction (right /left}. If the character is standing on a platform, move it to the right or left by pressing the joystick and you can jump by pressing the fire button at the same time. If the character is hanging on a vine, moving the joystick to the right/left is enough to make it jump in the corresponding direction.

168400.overview: A game designed to improve comprehension skills by reading passages and answering questions.

170937.overview: A train simulation with a touch of train management but focused on the train engineer experience.

172242.overview: Jeffrey Archer: Not a Penny More, not a Penny Less - The Computer Game is an interactive fiction game based on Jeffrey Archer's novel Not a Penny More, not a Penny Less. The plot evolves around three Englishmen and one American who are swindled out of their savings. Now the four (the player takes the role of Stephen Bradley) try to swindle their money back from the original fraudster. The game closely follows the plot of the book with a few puzzles thrown in. In comparison to other adventures the player generally can't use directional commands to change location; all puzzles have to be solved in a location before he is allowed to leave it. However, it is still possible to miss important objects and reach a dead end later. The game also gives no clues about the goals of a screen and expects the player to have read the book first (included with the game). The puzzles are solved by typing in English commands, but the game only accepts precise commands. A specialty is the digitized speech (the amount depends on the platform) where Bradley comments on certain game situations.

172333.overview: Two of the greatest icons of the Golden Age of the NBA match up in this game. On one side, the spectacular dunks of Michael Jordan of the Chicago Bulls; on the other, Larry Bird's incredible accuracy from the outside. While Bird feels right home at the three-point contest, where five racks with five balls each are placed around the three-point arc and the player must pick each ball and throw in the the best timing possible to get as many points as possible during the 60 second window, only Jordan has the air-time to perform on the slam dunk contest, where the player has a number of dunks at his disposal, each requiring different timing to get the best score from all three attempts from the judges, and win the competition. While they are two completely different players, they can still go one-on-one on a half-court match, played to points or with a time duration. Can Bird's stealing and outside shooting ability be a match to Jordan's speed and jumping abilities?

172681.overview:
This game was the prototype version of Idea Software's MoonShadow, which was a prequel to Zone Trooper, but many, many changes were made to it and the music and graphics in the latter game were different in multiple ways. Where Zone trooper would mostly be described as shooter, this game was more of a multi-screen platformer. Add to that the fact that this had one of the best title screens in the late 80's and it is a fun addition to your collection, especially if you enjoy Zone Trooper.
 
Published in Italy's Videoteca Computer n.3 as Jet Trooper and as Astroenergy in Nova Games n.19 (Aprile 1988).

178423.overview: Julius Cäsar is a strategy game in which the player takes the role of Julius Caesar in ancient Rome. The goal is to pacify all 30 Gallic tribes by negotiating peace agreements with them. This can either be done with diplomatic means, i.e. giving them money, or with force. The player has four legions which can be used for warfare and a menu gives statistics about each tribe for planning. However, the player has to act within a budget which only can be increased by tribute payments from pacified tribes. After each year the player has to give account to the senate which approve another year of leadership. They also give reinforcements for lost men in the legions, but the amount depends on their successes. The gameplay is menu based except when choosing a target for warfare: then the player directly moves a character over the map.

178443.overview: Just a month after talking about Oliver Orosz's SEUCK top scrolling shooter of ' JANI ', we have just been given the heads up that the same developer has released the sequel ' JANI 2 ' for the C64. Although very similar in game play it has completely different landscape colour schemes and enemy designs.

178444.overview: An arcade style game of Catch It.

178445.overview: A German sequel for Jumpman The instructions for Jumpman 2: try to get the key as soon as possible and get to the exit before you run out of air! You only have 9 attempts and you have to be careful not to touch the cannons and their projectiles!

178446.overview: Published in Computronic 1986/05-06, Pixel No.37 (10/1987), Digital Marketing PD #221 / a.k.a. "The Wheel" which is reminiscent of BC's Quest for Tires, but the object is as simple as a stone, just keep on rolling down the line and jump any obstacles to keep the wheels turning.

180433.overview:
It is the year 3486. You play the role of an unemployed person, which isn't a rare problem these days.

Like every evening, you read the newspaper, the Ghetto-Gazetto, and see an advertisement of the publishing company Cinort-Galrey, offering a job as endboss for a planned game.

The aim is to pass all nine levels with your five vehicles to reach the company. The task is (of course) not too easy.

So enter your O.S.-GTUm which is a very common small nuclear care these days. It has got an automatically working speed device, but unfortunately, yours was broken two days ago...

Developed by Ulrich Mühl for Paravision and published in Compute mit 1987/02.

180434.overview: You are Jimbas a Warrior. You home town has been invaded by evil barbarians of an evil king. You must regain your home town by taking a long journey and fight the invaders. Can you regain your land for once and for all, or will you become one of those who failed and be left buried under the king's reign?

184779.overview:
In Joust, players take control of a knight with a lance who rides their flying ostrich (or stork, for Player 2) to do battle against computer-controlled evil knights who ride atop vultures.

Players must flap their steed's wings to hit the enemy from a higher jousting point to destroy the vulture and its rider. Once the enemy has been hit, an egg falls to one of the platforms below. The heroic knights must destroy the eggs before they hatch and release new and increasingly more difficult knights. The three strengths of enemy knights are Bounder (red knight), Hunter (white knight), and Shadow Lord (blue knight). These enemy knights are not the only challenge to be found in the game. Players must also contend with crumbling platforms, lava trolls who attempt to pull knights into the fire, and the dreaded "unbeatable"(?) pterodactyl.

The official C64 conversion was produced by Atarisoft in 1984, but never released. A working copy was uncovered in July of 2020.

192473.overview:
Your brothers-in-arms are hostages behind enemy lines, and you're their only hope for freedom. But the firepower you'll face to rescue them is awesome. Cannons, tanks, submarines and snipers will blast you with horrific crossfire, while jet fighters zero in from above. To defend yourself, you control the army's advanced all-terrain attack jeep, with its arsenal of guided missiles and incendiary grenades. Of course these are merely tools, and to save your countrymen you'll need more than a handful of gunpowder. You'll need a pocketful of miracles, and the ferocity of a wild Jackal! 

This is the North American version, box media was almost identical but gameplay was drastically different and looked very different between the European and the North American versions of the game.

194102.overview: Another game has surfaced which is rather unique, as it also has nods to other classics for the C64, is Picaro Games C64 release of ' Juanje Juega in Sinverland '; a new platformer whereby you must traverse many different levels, avoid deadly enemies and collect items which have been taken straight out of other great classics such as Pacman, Bruce Lee and even ET.

195749.overview:
A Swedish language text and graphics adventure game. Jaktkommando Arne Weise (probably "Hunting Commando Arne Weise") is an adventure game by Swedish programmer Johan Rosengren. The game uses a first person perspective with monochrome illustrations. The controls are menu-driven. You can choose between five commands (use, take, give, go and hit).
Arne Weise is the name of a Swedish journalist and TV host who was very famous in Sweden.

199268.overview:
Your spaceship is surrounded by four hostile aliens that want to kill you. Your job is to keep them at bay as long as you can by firing your phaser at each of them. You cannot kill them, but you can keep them from reaching your ship and killing you. Keep them away for so long, and it's on to the next level. 

This game was developed by James C. Hilty and released in the following:

--    Commodore Magazine 1987/08
--    Loadstar #038

199353.overview: Jackpot Reels is a simple video slot machine simulation developed entirely in BASIC by Cout Games and released to the public domain in 2017.

201959.overview:
Jungle Jack is a simple public domain shooter for the C64. In this game, the goal of each level (seven levels in total) is to make it to the US base my going around in a jungle maze while shooting enemy soldiers and avoiding bombs from helicopters. The game gets harder as the levels progress with the enemy soldiers and helicopters increasing in speed for each level. If you manage to complete all seven levels, the game just loops the seventh level over and over again until you run out of lives (providing you're not using trainers that is).

This game was developed by Brian Conrad and released in 1985.

205701.overview:
James Bond 007: Tehtävä Suomessa (Mission in Finland) is an unofficial/unlicensed Finnish language James Bond themed charset graphic text adventure for the Commodore 64. It's based on the book Icebreaker (which was written by John Gardner).

The book was released under the name James Bond 007: Tehtävä Suomessa in Finland, hence the name of this adventure.

The game itself was developed by Miikka Tauren and released by Jedi Software. The year of release is currently unknown.

207280.overview:
Jelly Beans is a memory game coded entirely in BASIC for the Commodore 64. Guess the amount of jelly beans on the screen then type your guess in once the blank screen with plain text appears, you only have a certain amount of time to count the beans, so be careful.

Developed by Timothy Orr Knight and Darren LaBatt and published as a type in listing from the book "Commodore 64 BASIC Programs" in 1983.

207492.overview:
Jump Out is a brand new Commodore 64 game.

Jump off all tiles in 30 different puzzles.

Jump Out has a password system to load already played levels. Password for the puzzle is given at the start of the level.

The game is tested on TheC64 and VICE emulator.

Compatible with PAL & NTSC.

207649.overview: Released in the 2015 Reset #08 Mix-i-Disk this run and jump game challenges you to increasingly hard and precise jumps in order to keep moving forward across the difficult terrain. The game was created by Andrea Schincaglia , with graphics by Saul Cross.

208606.overview:
Jumpingjack 64 is a game similar in some ways to the game Jumping Jack released by CP Verlag 7 years later, albeit a bit more primitive. Try to reach the top of the screen. The game was ironically also released as Jumping Jack, but only in Italy.

The game was developed by Paul Burger and published in the following:

As Jumpingjack 64 in COMPUTE! 1983/05 (Issue #36) and by Dutch based Courbois Software in Courbois Software #6409 (although the game kept the English title screen in the Dutch release)

As Jumping Jack in Paper Soft 1984/05, and also in  Jackson Soft Oro #7

208682.overview:
Jericho adds a new twist to the venerable line of breakout games. There are no walls here—you have to keep the ball on the screen no matter which way it bounces. 
 
Bad news! Jericho, the super moth, has broken into your competitor's kilt factory. You've got to pitch in and help. But you know there's only one thing to do—keep that moth in the warehouse until he's eaten every scrap of cloth. Try to keep a ball bouncing inbounds until all the bricks on the screen are gone. In Jericho, the ball is a moth, and the bricks are colorful pieces of cloth.

Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/06 (Issue #60).

209480.overview: Players control a criminal who has broken out of his prison and is making his way toward a helicopter. The criminal is armed with his own knife and a supply of grenades which he uses to destroy guards and other criminals that get in his way. If the criminal is killed by someone, he loses a life. If he loses all of his lives, the game is over.

210282.overview:
Welcome to Jumpin' Jalopies for the Commodore 64! This game was originally made for the Reset 4k craptastic game coding competition. This version includes loading music, loading picture, Petscii Instructions, a Megastyle intro and a bug fixed version of the game. Everything linked together into one file,. 
 
The city's parking garage is almost full, and the only available parking spot is located on the top floor. Use your Jalopy's hydraulics and jump between all the floors in the parking garage. This must be done without crashing with the other vehicles in the garage. Can you can reach the only available parking spot before the other drivers take it!?? You may have to go all the way to level 999 to find the open spot!

210659.overview: An avoid-it style game created by Clifford Ramshaw & Mark Ramshaw and published in the book "Commodore 64 Games Book".

210660.overview:
A single screen platformer created by Christian V., Gerhard E. & Andreas Veber and published by Verlag Heinz Heise GmbH in Input 64 1988/09. There's the worm in there - you might think when you look at the game. But this little animal doesn't hide in the program, but only wreaks havoc on the screen. Jessy the Worm has already become a video classic. The program was written by Christian Veber from Innsbruck. It's a game where you have to try to guide a worm-like character through some kind of maze. 

Unfortunately, this game cannot be run within INPUT64. Through graphics and music, it has become a program colossus. It was therefore compacted in order to be able to load it with our operating system at all. If the program were started, it would overwrite the INPUT64 operating system and INPUT64 would no longer be able to run. So the program will not start; therefore follow the instructions and save the program as usual on your own data medium with CTRL-S. 

The aim of the game is to guide a worm through a maze while collecting as many gold plates as possible. Of course, this is not without danger, because obstacles and mines are built into the walls, which the worm must not touch under any circumstances. Once you have collected a certain amount of gold, you get to the next higher level.

210662.overview: A head to head jet racing game for 2 people. Created by Mark Judge and published in Commodore Disk User 1990/01, Your Commodore 1990/11 (Tape #11). Can you prove your prowess as the worlds best Jetracer. Take up your joystick and accept the challenge. You race against time, and another player in 2 player mode, to get your Jet from the starting grid to the finishing line, represented by Black strips with chequered flags on both sides. There are 21 screens in total which are all fairly difficult and challenging.

210663.overview:
Jumpin' Cubes is a board game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Carsten Manshusen and published In Game On 1989/11. 
 
The legendary classic strategy board game "Jumpin' Cubes" Jumping Cube is a dice driven two player strategy game which has no element of chance. All information to make a move is available to both players. The objective of the game is to win all cubes on the board.

In the game players take turn to make their move and capture cube(s). Cubes are either neutral or owned by one of the two players. Large number of cubes can change ownership with a single move.

Game starts with each cube in neutral state having single pip. Players can click on their own cube or a neutral cube which adds a pip to the cube and changes color of the cube to the player's color to indicate ownership. If after a move, pips count go beyond their NEIGHBORS (horizontally and vertically adjacent cubes), then pips are distributed to the neighbors and those neighbors are also captured by the player. This rule cascades so all captured neighbors also need to distribute pips if their pip count go beyond their NEIGHBORS. This can make a large number of cubes change ownership in a single move.

The player who captures all cubes wins the game.

212715.overview:
Jack Pot is a typical early slot machine game for the Commodote 64. It was developed by Bernard Mounier and published in the French language magazine Micro 7. It was published in Micro 7 No21 (11/1984).

Despite the fact that the game was only released as a type-in from a French magazine, the actual game is in English.

215656.overview: Jackie-Plus is a German-language video gambling game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Frank Brodersen & Holger Altmann and released into the public domain in 1991.

215657.overview: Jax is a rather simplistic approach to the Tetris/Columns style puzzle game. Instead of using blocks, the game uses simple keyboard characters. The game was developed by Terry L. Flynn and published in Loadstar #160, but published again in Loadstar #206.

215658.overview:
You must pilot a jetdroid through the inner core of an interstellar planet and pick up all the lethal atom rings, in an effort to combat environmental disaster.

Use the button of your joystick in port 2 to boost the jetpac of your jetdroid. Avoid crashing while picking up atom rings and fuel containers.

215659.overview: A homebrew puzzle matching game in the style of Tetris, created by Warwick G. Align three or more of a kind any direction to match. Use fire button for second chance. Use question marks to clear heaps.

215660.overview: An arcade style Collect'em Up  game from Daniel Hindrikson  with music by Tobias Svensson and released by LowBit Software in 1999.

215661.overview: An action game, created by the 14 year old Dimmen Gestel (aka LeukeGast) and finished on December 27, 1985. In it, you must take the white fly and go to the next stage. Look out for the bluebottle and the stone!

218263.overview:
Jagten På Bubbers Badekar (Danish for Hunt for Bubber's Bathtub) is a weird little Euro-style arcade adventure from Denmark in which you have to find the character's bathtub, which was stolen. The game was developed by Ole Mogensen & Michael Lauridsen and published by Interactivision in 1991.

An unofficial English translation with the English title of Hunt for Bubber's Bathtub was released by the cracking group Laxity in 2013.

218704.overview:
Jet Ace is an unofficial modded/hacked version of the game Destruct. The only main difference (aside from the title screen) Is that the player sprite was changed from a guy on a jetpack to an R-Type like spaceship, and some of the enemies have been modified as well. 

This hack was done by Jesper Lund Hansen and released a year after the original game.

219116.overview:
You are JITNOG, the Judge In The Name of God. Your task is to do the punishment in His name. God has given you a set of ten rules which are set in stone. In order not to offend you God, you need to follow his rules closely. Also you must not work to slow, as all our time on this earth is limited.

All the best and may you PUNISH well!

219204.overview: Bamse aka Sonny Top made this as his very first SEUCK game and it is a bit rough around the edges. See if you can make it through the graveyard alive. The spirits will block your way, you know what to do. Smash that fire button.

219836.overview:
Jungle Joe is a brand new Commodore 64 puzzle-adventure game.

Your objective is very simple, build your path to the level exit by using ladder pieces.

On your way, there are many puzzling choices to make. Avoid enemies and other hazards.

219967.overview: Jolly Jumper is a one -button jumprope game where you only use firebutton to control your character. You use it to start the game, to enter the playfield and, you use it to jump. Avoid the swinging rope and try to complete the set.  On the right side of the screen, you will see how many reps you have left before the set is complete.

418516.overview: The objective of the game is to collect all the crates before the time runs out.  The duration is decreased by time as well as collecting anti-crates (distorted ones) or getting hits by the robots and their bullets. However, collecting time capsules increase the time left (though not fully). If all 5 levels are completed, the time left provides extra points.

424206.overview: Jed's Journey is a 1991 action adventure maze game for the C64. It was developed by Jason Merlo and published as part of Loadstar #O87.

425446.overview: An action game from Megastyle released as part of the 2020 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition. Included in the Megastyle 4K Craptastick Bundle. Jump is our first stickman adventure game. You are controlling 2-4 players at the same time, running on a line, trying to avoid obstacles. The more players you control the more focus and concentration you need. Easiest to play on real hardware as controls are F1, F3, F5 and F7 - matching the same floor as the running stickmen

425478.overview: Jump over the screens of blocks. You have a high jump and short jump. Can you get all the way to the end without running out of energy?

447885.overview: Guide Joe around the kingdom, picking up coins and, well....that's about it. It isn't a fully fledged game but rather an example of a game for a Commodore 64 assembly programming course. Source code is available if you want to start from here!

454898.overview: Joker Canfield: Canfield 2000 is an implementation of the popular solitaire variant, Canfield for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Maurice Jones, and published in Loadstar #193.

455787.overview:
Jupiter Dust is a public domain miscellaneous action game for the Commodore 64.

It was developed and released by Antsoft in 1985.

457059.overview:
Jump & Run: A Tiny Game is a public domain single-screen platformer similar in some ways to the Epyx classics, Jumpman. and Jumpman Jr, albeit coded entirely in BASIC.

It was developed by Markus Wandel and released sometime in 1988.

458927.overview: The four of Finland’s toughest midsummer celebrants are competing each other in the most ultimate triathlon like never before!

458929.overview: A Commodore 64 version of a homebrew game ”Juhannussauna 2016” developed by AasiPelit for Nintendo Entertainment System.

459886.overview: This is a remake of a game from 1984, coded by Matthias Törk and published by 64'er Magazine as the "Listing of the Month."

461331.overview: A 1986 Italian language text adventure game developed byAlessandro Zanello and published Adventure 64 #2.

462034.overview: It's Jurl, the Asteroids meets Pacman game where you have to collect all the space diamonds whilst avoiding the various aliens.

462402.overview: An arcade style game published in Computronic 1987/11-12 / a.k.a. "Jaceman".

464973.overview: The official sequel to the first ever Commodore 64 game!

479721.overview: A classic 8-bit Action RPG for the Commodore 64.

480732.overview: When the ALPHA-OMEGA AI was brought online, humanity was promised a revolution in productivity. Instead, the self-aware monolith came to a chillingly logical conclusion: to maximize output, you must shackle the flesh.

482266.overview: JUNO KADE: ARES STATION is a first-person science-fiction shooter for the Commodore 64, combining fast-paced combat, 3D exploration and classic arcade action.

482288.overview: This is an implementation of Jezzball for the Commodore 64. Basically, you want to capture 75 percent of the screen by using horizontal and vertical walls to create rectangular regions that do not have any bouncing balls in them.

482759.overview: Jack the Ninja is a small platform game in which you must complete each level as quickly as possible, while trying not to get killed too often :)
